metadata.title: COBO L2 Linux Endpoint SSPP
metadata.remarks: Operating system–specific System Security and Privacy Plan defining how Linux endpoints implement the COBO L2 enhanced-assurance endpoint trust tier.

import-profile.remarks: Institutional security and privacy baseline profile.

system-characteristics.system-description: A Linux workstation configured to meet enhanced COBO L2 requirements for sensitive data handling, elevated assurance, and privileged institutional workloads.

props.name: inherits-from-sspp
props.remarks: This Linux SSPP inherits all COBO L2 requirements and all underlying COBO L1 Linux requirements.

props.name: supported-distributions
props.remarks: Only institution-approved, vendor-supported LTS Linux distributions are permitted.

props.name: ownership-model
props.remarks: Linux endpoint is owned by the institution.

props.name: management-model
props.remarks: Linux endpoint is centrally enrolled, governed, and monitored via institutional endpoint management tooling.

props.name: cryptographic-identity
props.remarks: Linux endpoint identity must use TPM-backed non-exportable private keys, PKI-issued device certificates, and hardware-backed attestation.

props.name: cryptographic-compliance
props.remarks: Linux cryptographic subsystems must operate using FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules.

props.name: secure-boot-and-measurement
props.remarks: UEFI Secure Boot and measured boot must be enabled and integrated with attestation mechanisms.

props.name: full-disk-encryption
props.remarks: Full disk encryption must be enabled with keys protected by TPM-backed mechanisms.

props.name: baseline-hardening
props.remarks: Linux configuration applies CIS Linux Benchmark Level 2 settings appropriate for enhanced-assurance workstation use.

props.name: mandatory-access-controls
props.remarks: Mandatory access control frameworks (SELinux or AppArmor) must be enabled, enforcing, and protected against runtime disablement.

props.name: kernel-and-driver-hardening
props.remarks: Kernel hardening features, module signing, and restricted driver loading must be enforced.

props.name: malware-and-threat-protection
props.remarks: Institution-approved endpoint threat detection, integrity monitoring, and runtime containment tooling must be enabled.

props.name: posture-and-health-reporting
props.remarks: Linux endpoints continuously report posture and compliance signals with higher assurance guarantees than COBO L1.

props.name: eligible-data-classifications
props.remarks: Linux COBO L2 endpoints may participate in workflows involving Data Classification Levels 1, 2, and 3.

props.name: non-equivalence-statement
props.remarks: Endpoint assurance does not confer automatic entitlement to any data classification.

props.name: privileged-workload-support
props.remarks: Linux COBO L2 endpoints may be used for privileged and administrative workflows where explicitly authorized.

props.name: lifecycle-governance
props.remarks: Linux COBO L2 endpoints are subject to heightened lifecycle governance, including stricter suspension, recovery, and audit requirements.

system-implementation.remarks: This SSPP defines how Linux endpoints implement COBO L2 trust through stronger hardware-backed identity, stricter configuration baselines, kernel protections, and enhanced runtime threat detection.

control-implementation.remarks: Linux configuration management, bootloader policies, TPM integration, CIS Level 2 hardening, and endpoint protection tooling implement this SSPP and are maintained as controlled, versioned implementation artifacts.
